topic: GNP vs GDP: territory vs a country's people, net factor income from abroad (shown as 'NFIAD') with its three listed parts and India's sign for each, and why India's GNP comes out below its GDP

concepts.name: GDP vs GNP: territory vs the country's people
GNP formula and NFIA
concepts.prereq_recalled: GDP as output inside the territory

concepts.name: three listed parts of NFIA
concepts.prereq_recalled: NFIA as income of Indians abroad minus income of foreigners in India

concepts.name: private remittance: earning abroad and sending money home
net remittances: plus in, minus out; mostly positive for India
interest on external loans: paid is minus, earned is plus; mostly negative for India
external grants: no interest; given is minus, received is plus
net NFIA negative, so India's GNP is below GDP

book_understanding.teaching_order: A textbook gives GNP = GDP + NFIA, defines NFIA as factor income earned abroad by residents minus factor income earned here by non-residents, and lists its parts. The video first builds a world of country boxes and people dots, lets a GDP/GNP button filter it, and writes the formula only after the picture; then it names NFIA and walks each part with a story and a pair of opposite flows (in = plus, out = minus) with small numbers, keeping a running sign on a hub. The verdict about India (GNP below GDP) is earned by adding the signs back into the formula. A film scene closes it instead of a recap.
book_understanding.breakdown_rule: Split the net figure into its parts; for each part show one inflow and one outflow with small numbers, give India's net sign, then add the signs back into the formula.

talmel_summary: Speech and picture fit closely: most changes land within about a second of their word, and the picture shows the idea rather than writing it (the GDP/GNP buttons filter the dots, money arrows run in and out with plus and minus badges, the minus badge drops into the formula and flips the sign). Numbers appear on the arrows several seconds before they are read. Weak spots: a 16-s transcript gap over the Jassi/Alberto scene, a brand-logo story, NDP/NNP shown but never spoken, and a 35-s film clip with real actors and no transcribed speech.

voice.notes: Friendly, clear Hinglish with English economic terms; 'maan lijiye' opens each scene and 'aap' puts the learner inside the story. Numbers are read as plain arithmetic ('5000 minus 2000 which is equals to 3000 rupees'). A refrain after each part ('positive bhi ho sakta hai aur negative bhi', then India's usual sign) gives the video its rhythm. Light humour at the end; no recap.

game_ideas.player_does: sees country boxes full of coloured people-dots at work and taps whose income counts in India's GDP and whose in India's GNP
game_ideas.process_happens: each tapped dot's income coin flies into a GDP jar or a GNP jar; a foreign engineer working in India goes into GDP but not GNP; an Indian nurse working in the Gulf goes into GNP but not GDP
game_ideas.win: both jars are right and the gap between them equals NFIA
game_ideas.lose: putting the Indian working abroad into GDP lights up the foreign box's border: GDP is about the land, not the passport
game_ideas.concept: GDP vs GNP: territory vs the country's people

game_ideas.player_does: runs India's external account for a year as event cards arrive (an Indian abroad sends ₹5000 home, a foreign worker in India sends ₹2000 out, ₹2000 interest is due to the World Bank, a neighbour pays ₹1000 interest, India gives a ₹500 grant) and routes each coin along the right arrow
game_ideas.process_happens: coins move into or out of the India map; each arm of the hub keeps a running net with a plus or minus badge; at year end the net badge flies into GNP = GDP + NFIA and the GNP bar settles above or below the GDP bar
game_ideas.win: player predicts the net sign and whether GNP ends above or below GDP before the reveal
game_ideas.lose: routing interest paid as an inflow pushes GNP above GDP; the replay shows which arrow ran the wrong way
game_ideas.concept: net factor income and India's GNP vs GDP (use whichever list of parts BIE adopts after checking the definitions)

game_ideas.player_does: marks which statements are wrong: 'GNP is always lower than GDP', 'GNP = GDP - NFIA when NFIA is negative', 'remittances are always positive', 'grants carry interest'
game_ideas.process_happens: each marked statement opens a small replay of the arrows or the formula that proves or breaks it
game_ideas.win: player explains that GNP < GDP only when NFIA is negative and that the sign already sits inside NFIA
game_ideas.lose: accepting 'always lower' plays a case with positive NFIA where GNP rises above GDP
game_ideas.concept: sign logic of GNP = GDP + NFIA

notes_questions.q: GDP aur GNP mein basic farak kya hai: zameen (territory) ya log (nationals)?
GNP ka formula kya hai, aur NFIA kaise nikaalte hain?
Video ke hisaab se NFIA ke teen hisse kaun se hain, aur India ke liye har ek ka sign kya hota hai?
Private remittance kya hai? US mein kaam karne wala Indian paise ghar kaise bhejta hai?
Agar ₹5000 India aaye aur ₹2000 bahar gaye, to net remittances kitne hue?
India ka GNP aam taur par GDP se kam kyon rehta hai?

checks_learned: Check definitions against standard national accounts before reuse: NFIA is net factor income (compensation of employees, interest, dividends, profits); remittances and grants are current transfers. Flag lists that put transfers inside factor income.
Check acronyms against standard usage (screen 'NFIAD' vs usual 'NFIA').
Flag 'always' or 'never' when the same narration earlier said 'mostly'.
A sign shown in a formula must keep the algebra consistent: if NFIA is negative, write GNP = GDP + NFIA or GDP minus its size, not GDP - NFIA.
When parts of a net figure are taught, each part should get the same pattern (one inflow, one outflow, small numbers, net); flag a part that breaks the pattern (grants had no numbers).
Rows shown on screen but never spoken (NDP, NNP) should be marked 'coming next' or removed.
Live-action film clips and real company or bank logos cannot be reused; replace with generic characters and generic company/bank shapes.
Transcript gaps over 10 s during teaching must be re-transcribed before talmel scoring (152-168 s here).

teaching_best.why: a 'maan lijiye' world of boxes and dots makes territory vs people concrete before any formula
GDP and GNP as two buttons that filter the same picture: the definition becomes a switch
each part gets an inflow, an outflow, small numbers and a net, then its sign goes onto the hub
the verdict about India is earned by adding the signs, not just stated

teaching_weak.why: a 70-s brand-name story for one idea; real logos cannot be reused
remittances and grants presented as factor income (doubtful; describe, verify)
the recap is handed to a 35-s film clip with real actors and no transcribed speech
the grants part has no numbers, breaking the pattern set by the first two parts
